records.name: Sufficient statistic
records.summary: A statistic whose value leaves the conditional distribution of the full sample free of the parameter.
records.statistical_question_answered: Can the data be reduced without losing parameter information under the model?
assumptions_required: A parametric family and statistic are specified.
conditions_required: Conditional distribution of sample given statistic does not depend on θ.
guarantees: The statistic contains all model information about θ in the sufficiency sense.
does_not_guarantee: It does not mean causal sufficiency or lossless prediction for unrelated targets.
do_not_use_when: When the model is misspecified or statistic is for a different parameter.
diagnostic_questions: Does the conditional distribution depend on θ?

records.name: Minimal sufficient statistic
records.summary: A sufficient statistic that is a function of every other sufficient statistic.
records.statistical_question_answered: What is the coarsest parameter-preserving reduction?
records.problem_addressed: Identifies maximal data compression under the model.
records.decision_improved: Improves efficient representation and estimator conditioning.
assumptions_required: At least one sufficient statistic exists.
does_not_guarantee: It does not guarantee low dimension or ease of use.
do_not_use_when: When model support or likelihood ratios are mishandled.
common_misuses: Assuming a sufficient statistic is automatically minimal.
diagnostic_questions: Can every sufficient statistic recover this one?
checks_or_evidence_needed: Likelihood ratio criterion or function argument.

records.name: Ancillary statistic
records.summary: A statistic whose distribution does not depend on the parameter.
records.statistical_question_answered: Which observed feature carries no parameter information in its marginal distribution?
records.problem_addressed: Supports conditional reasoning about precision and Basu-type independence.
records.decision_improved: Improves recognition of information-free but precision-relevant summaries.
assumptions_required: Parametric model and statistic are specified.
guarantees: Statistic has no marginal parameter information.
does_not_guarantee: It is not necessarily irrelevant to conditional inference.
do_not_use_when: When its distribution depends on θ or nuisance parameters.
common_misuses: Dismissing ancillary information without considering conditioning.
diagnostic_questions: Does the distribution depend on any unknown parameter?
checks_or_evidence_needed: Distribution derivation or simulation under θ values.

records.name: Complete statistic
records.summary: A statistic family is complete when a zero expectation for all parameter values forces the function to be zero almost surely.
records.statistical_question_answered: Can unbiased functions of a statistic be unique?
records.problem_addressed: Provides the uniqueness engine for best unbiased estimators.
assumptions_required: A family of distributions for T is specified.
conditions_required: The zero-expectation implication holds for all θ.
guarantees: Unbiased estimators based on T are unique.
does_not_guarantee: Completeness is model-specific and not automatic.
do_not_use_when: Curved or restricted families lacking completeness.
diagnostic_questions: Does Eθ g(T)=0 for all θ imply g(T)=0?
checks_or_evidence_needed: Known theorem or proof for the family.

records.name: Likelihood function
records.summary: The joint density or mass of the observed sample viewed as a function of the parameter.
records.statistical_question_answered: Which parameter values make the observed data relatively more compatible with the model?
records.problem_addressed: Centralizes data evidence for likelihood-based inference.
records.decision_improved: Improves estimation, testing, and data-reduction reasoning.
assumptions_required: A parametric model for the sample is specified.
conditions_required: Observed data are fixed while θ varies.
guarantees: Likelihood ratios and maxima can be computed up to parameter-free factors.
does_not_guarantee: It is not a probability distribution over θ by itself.
use_when: MLEs, LRTs, likelihood principle, Bayesian updating with priors.
do_not_use_when: When the sampling model is wrong or support restrictions are ignored.
diagnostic_questions: What is the joint model for the observed data?

records.conclusion: Parameter information in the sample is captured by T in the sufficiency sense.
records.proof_strategy_summary: Check conditional sample probabilities within level sets of T.

records.plain_language_meaning: A statistic is sufficient exactly when the joint density/mass factors into a parameter-dependent part through the statistic and a parameter-free part.
assumptions: The sample has a joint pdf or pmf with common dominating measure as used in the theorem.
conditions: The sample has a joint pdf or pmf with common dominating measure as used in the theorem.
records.conclusion: Sufficiency can be checked algebraically from the likelihood.
records.why_it_matters: This is the practical workhorse for finding sufficient statistics.
records.proof_strategy_summary: Show factorization implies parameter-free conditional distribution on statistic level sets and conversely construct factors.
common_misuse: Dropping θ-dependent support terms into h(x) incorrectly
what_breaks_if_assumptions_fail: A statistic may be falsely declared sufficient.

conditions: Support and zero-density cases are handled as in theorem.
records.conclusion: Minimal sufficient reductions can be identified by comparing likelihood ratios.
records.why_it_matters: This refines sufficiency to avoid redundant summaries.
records.proof_strategy_summary: Use the partition of sample space induced by parameter-free likelihood ratios and show it is the coarsest sufficient partition.

records.plain_language_meaning: In full exponential families with an open natural-parameter set, the natural sufficient statistic is complete under stated conditions.

conditions: Natural parameter set contains an open subset.
records.conclusion: Completeness can be established for many standard models.
records.why_it_matters: Enables Lehmann-Scheffe/BUE results in binomial, Poisson, normal-family cases.
records.proof_strategy_summary: Use uniqueness of transforms over an open parameter set.
